title: Refactor: decouple continuous-batcher and KV cache APIs to reduce tail-latency
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: This ticket scopes a non-disruptive refactor to separate concerns between the continuous batching scheduler and the KV cache lifecycle. Over time the two systems have become tightly coupled: batcher timers reference cache internals and cache eviction logic triggers scheduler backoffs. That coupling increases tail latency and makes micro-optimizations high-risk. Goals: 1) introduce a minimal, stable interface boundary between the continuous-batcher and KV cache (Batcher -> CacheClient interface), 2) centralize eviction policy config and expose signals instead of internal callbacks, 3) remove synchronous blocking calls from hot scheduler paths, 4) add unit and integration tests to validate no-regression under production-like load profiles, and 5) ship behind a runtime feature-flag with canary rollout.

Acceptance criteria: - Batcher reads/writes KV cache only via CacheClient interface (no direct internal type imports) - Scheduler hot path has zero synchronous IO (all eviction/checks async or batched) - Tail P95/P99 latency for generation requests at representative traffic reduces by at least 10% on the canary cluster, or does not regress (pass/fail check) - All new code covered by unit tests and an integration test that simulates mixed sequence length workload - Feature flag supports per-cluster enablement and automatic rollback on SLO breach.

Non-goals: Full redesign of eviction heuristics (this is out of scope) and changes to persistent KV-backed caches. This work focuses on in-memory KV cache and scheduler interactions.

Implementation plan: 1) Spike (2d): design CacheClient minimal surface (get_prefix, put_prefix, async_eviction_signal) and update design doc. 2) Implement adapter in runtime that implements CacheClient and delegates to existing cache (3d). 3) Replace batcher direct calls with CacheClient usage (2d), ensure compilation and behavior parity. 4) Move eviction decision logic behind an async queue and expose eviction signals consumed by a separate eviction worker (4d). 5) Add integration test harness that replays production trace with synthetic timing (2d). 6) Canary rollout to low-traffic region; compare latency and error rates (2d). 7) Full rollout and retrospective.

Rollout/runbook: - Enable feature flag on canary cluster (us-west-2-canary) with 1/10 traffic. - Monitor trace SLOs (P95/P99), error rates, and throughput for 48 hours. - If SLO regressions exceed 5% relative to baseline for 30 minutes, auto-disable and revert using the feature flag. - Post-mortem and follow-ups if any anomalies.

Risk and mitigation: - Risk: subtle race between eviction worker and batcher leading to cache misses. Mitigation: strict ordering guarantees in CacheClient and additional integration tests simulating races. - Risk: performance regressions in adapter layer. Mitigation: microbenchmarks before canary and use fast-path inline helpers.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Decouple+Batcher+and+KV+Cache, spike notes: drive link to docs, performance bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Agreed to keep surface minimal to reduce touch area. Assigned prototype to Marco.

2026-03-01 - Marco Li: Completed spike. Posted CacheClient interface sketch and benchmark plan. Found one blocker: current cache eviction uses thread-local timers that expect synchronous callbacks. Proposed async queue approach in design doc.
2026-03-04 - Samir Patel (code review): Reviewed adapter changes. Requested removal of blocking futures on hot path and suggested using a lock-free ring buffer for eviction signals.
2026-03-06 - Marco Li: Implemented adapter and updated batcher to call CacheClient. CI green on unit tests. Microbenchmarks show no measurable CPU overhead on hot paths.

2026-03-08 - QA (Priya Rao): Integration harness added with production trace replay. Noted intermittent cache miss spike in scenario with many short sequences; pushed test improvements to reproduce consistently.
2026-03-10 - Marco Li: Added eviction worker and race tests. Preparing canary rollout. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2219
2026-03-12 - Product (Lena Morales): Reviewed rollout plan and SLO thresholds. Approved canary for us-west-2-canary. Reminder: notify infra for quota allocation.
2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Feature flag ready. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-14. Next steps: run bench vs baseline and capture traces for analysis.
